causal_chain.claim: orders scheduled retries of payment calls with zero backoff
payments returned temporarily_unavailable errors in response to those calls
gateway observed upstream_timeout errors when calling orders

root_cause.summary: orders retries calls to payments repeatedly without backoff, amplifying load on payments

verification.reason: disabling the matching condition(s) makes the incident disappear

alternatives.why_less_likely: Payments latency increase was moderate and could be a side-effect of retry-driven load; no evidence of payments deploy or resource exhaustion.
Orders worker saturation is a symptom of the retry amplification; the underlying cause is the retry behavior, not an intrinsic loss of capacity.

causal_chain.claim: Orders retried payment calls with zero backoff upon receiving 503 responses.
This immediate retry increased load on the payments service.
Increased payments load led to higher latency and error rates, causing orders calls to payments to stall or fail.
Gateway timed out waiting for responses from the slow orders service.
Gateway timeouts resulted in 5xx errors and elevated latency observed in gateway metrics.

root_cause.summary: Orders service retried payment calls immediately upon failure, amplifying load and causing downstream overload.
